subject: Intermittent edge-proxy backpressure impacting live chat — initial report and remediation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <ops@rallyworks.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat responses slowing / token drip starting ~08:45 PT

Hi Dylan —

We're seeing a pronounced slowdown on our live chat integration starting ~08:45 PT this morning. Responses are arriving in bursts and sometimes stall for 6–10s before any tokens appear. The client-side shows normal request rates (no retry storms) and overall TPS looks flat. This is impacting user-facing chats on our morning peak and one of our largest customer segments is seeing timeouts.

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something we should change in our SDK? I captured a HAR and some telemetry, attaching a short trace.

Summary:
- Impact: ~15% of interactive sessions show token delay >6s
- First observed: 08:45 PT (2026-04-22)
- SDK: webchat-js v2.3.1, single-connection streaming
- Attached: client_trace_0848.har (included)

Appreciate a quick read on whether you can fall back to non-streaming while you triage.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Platform Engineer, RallyWorks

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <ops@rallyworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 09:34:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat responses slowing / token drip starting ~08:45 PT

Samir —

Thanks for the report and the HAR. We are seeing correlated signals in our edge-proxy metrics that indicate elevated request queue depth and delayed chunk delivery for the routing path that serves your region. Our initial mitigation is to route affected sessions to a fallback instance class that uses a more aggressive flush cadence; that will reduce the tail latency but may slightly alter per-token throughput.

Immediate actions I am initiating now:
- Promote temporary route with faster flush settings for your account (in progress, should complete <10m).
- Recommend RallyWorks enable client fallback to short-polling for sessions that detect >3s gap between tokens (SDK configurable, see steps below).
- I've attached an edge-proxy diagnostic bundle request — can you share the server times for the captured trace (we need the server-side timestamps from your HAR).

Quick SDK fallback guidance (client-side):
1) Detect token gap >3000ms.
2) If gap detected, close streaming ws and issue a POST to the non-stream endpoint to fetch remainder.
3) On reconnect, use lastMessageId to continue.

I will loop in Marissa and Kim to get a deeper look at kernel scheduling and queueing in the proxy layer. I'll follow up with a shortpostmortem and recommended durable mitigations.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 09:40:05 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Live chat responses slowing / token drip starting ~08:45 PT

Marissa / Kim —

Forwarding RallyWorks report. TL;DR: client saw token drip and stalls starting 08:45 PT that aligns with a spike in queue depth across a subset of our edge proxies in us-west-2. Initial mitigation: temporary route with faster flush cadence applied for their tenant which should blunt the tail but is a stop-gap.

Attachments: I requested a diagnostic bundle; I also attached our own edge metrics snapshot (edge-proxy-diagnostics-20260422.tar.gz) and a quick temporary-fallback-playbook.md that I applied.

Questions we need to answer in the next 4 hours:
- Root cause: is this backpressure originating from kernel-level batching or a transient upstream imbalance (LB misconfiguration)?
- Scope: are other customers on the same routing ring impacted? Early signals show a small cohort (~4%) but we need a full ring query.
- Durable fix: change proxy flush heuristics and add a short-circuit when queue depth crosses a threshold + auto-fallback.

Immediate asks for you:
- Marissa: can you run a packet-level sweep and confirm whether SYN/ACK pacing for chunked responses is present? See INF-4123.
- Kim: please validate the kernel selectors for the current edge build and whether the new commit we rolled last week could have altered the batching window.

I'll coordinate comms; once we have a concise cause and ETA I'll draft a customer-facing postmortem.

Thanks — will update in thread.

--
Dylan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <ops@rallyworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Incident summary & next steps — edge proxy backpressure (RallyWorks)

Samir —

Thanks again for the quick report and for sharing the HAR. Below is a concise incident summary, the immediate mitigations we applied, and the follow-up actions we will take. We appreciate your patience and your help with the traces.

What happened
- On 2026-04-22 08:45 PT an operational shift in proxy scheduling coincided with a burst of long-poll connections from a third-party integration; the combination increased queue depth on a small set of edge proxies in us-west-2. Queue depth grew to the point where chunk flushes were delayed, causing token drip and observable stalls for ~15% of streaming sessions for ~1h.

Immediate mitigations (applied 22 Apr)
- We routed your tenant to a fallback proxy profile with a reduced batching window and more frequent flushes (reduction in token gap observed within 8–10m).
- Temporary auto-fallback option enabled for your account so the Redwood SDK will fall back to short-polling on gaps >3s (no SDK release required — config change only).
- Limited, targeted restart of the affected proxy pool to rebalance requests and clear transient queues.

Customer impact
- Affected period: 2026-04-22 08:45 PT — 2026-04-22 09:52 PT
- Sessions impacted (estimate): ~15% of interactive sessions routed through the affected proxies
- Visible symptom: delayed token emission / intermittent stalls (6–10s gaps)

Root cause (summary)
- Contributing factors: an aggressive kernel batching heuristic introduced in the April 16 edge build combined with an unexpected surge from a third-party integration that concentrated load on a subset of proxies. The batching heuristic increased per-request queueing under specific traffic patterns.

Work we are doing (next steps)
- Engineering: Revert the aggressive batching heuristic for the edge build and roll a controlled patch to replace it with an adaptive heuristic (INF-4123, ETA 72 hours).
- Routing: Implement a probe that monitors queue depth per-proxy and triggers an automated fallback to the reduced-batching profile when threshold exceeded (ETA 5 business days).
- Observability: Add a dedicated alert for token-gap tail percentiles and a dashboard tile for per-tenant queue depth to make these signals visible in real time (ETA 3 business days).

Compensation & support
- We will apply a one-time service credit for the impacted usage window. Our support team will follow up with the specific credit amount and how it will appear on your bill.

Attachments included
- edge-proxy-diagnostics-20260422.tar.gz (proxy snapshots and logs)
- temporary-fallback-playbook.md (runbook we used for emergency route)

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute post-incident call tomorrow to walk through the diagnostic artifacts and the planned patch. Please let me know a time that works for your team.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the patch notes and a closure postmortem once INF-4123 is complete.

Best,
